prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Miami—best depends on your specific needs (complexity of the case, comfort with sedation, budget, location, aesthetic goals). Rather than a single name, here’s a short plan to find a top provider and what to look for.

Who typically places implants
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS) — handle complex surgery, sedation, bone grafting.  
- Periodontists — specialists in gums and implants.  
- Prosthodontists — specialists in replacing teeth and designing the crowns/bridges on implants.  
Often a team approach (surgeon + prosthodontist) gives the best functional and aesthetic result.

How to identify a strong implant clinician
- Proper training: DDS/DMD plus residency in oral surgery, periodontics, or prosthodontics, or advanced implant fellowship/courses.  
- Experience: number of implants placed and experience with cases like yours (single tooth vs full-arch).  
- Technology: in-office CBCT (3D imaging), guided implant planning, digital workflow.  
- Before/after photos and patient references.  
- Good communication: clear treatment plan, timeline, risks, alternatives, and written cost estimate.  
- Positive reviews on multiple platforms (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp).  
- Memberships/certifications: American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (if OMS), American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), or American Academy of Periodontology (AAP). Note: board certification is different from membership; both are useful signals.

Practical questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants have you placed? How many similar to my case?  
- Will you do the surgery and crown, or will another specialist do the crown?  
- Do you use CBCT scans and guided surgery?  
- Do I need bone grafting/sinus lift? If so, how often do you perform those?  
- What sedation options are available?  
- What is the timeline from implant placement to final crown?  
- What are the total costs (surgery, implant, abutment, crown, grafts, follow-ups)? Are payment plans available?  
- Do you offer a warranty/guarantee on the implant/restoration?

Typical cost range (ballpark)
- Single implant + abutment + crown in the U.S. commonly ranges roughly $2,000–$6,000 depending on materials and complexity. Complex cases (grafts, sinus lifts, full-arch) are more expensive.

How I can help right now
- If you tell me your Miami neighborhood or ZIP code, your budget/insurance, and whether you prefer an OMS, periodontist, or prosthodontist, I can find several highly rated local providers, with clinic links and what to ask at the first visit.

Resources to search on your own
- ADA Find-a-Dentist, AAID directory, ABOMS directory (for oral surgeons), Google/Healthgrades/Yelp patient reviews.

If you want, give me your ZIP or neighborhood and any preferences and I’ll pull a short list of well-reviewed implant specialists in Miami.
